description: Table 1 is a single-panel numeric data table (no axes, curves or graphics) reporting the calculated Zener-Hollomon parameter lnZ for Fe-Mn-Al–C steel as a function of deformation temperature and strain rate. The header is two-level: the stub column is labelled "\u03b5\u0307 (s⁻¹)" and the spanning head is "T (°C)", which splits into six temperature columns: 900, 950, 1000, 1050, 1100 and 1150. The four row entries are strain rates 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10 s⁻¹, so the table body contains 24 printed lnZ values. Every cell is legible and filled; no empty or missing entries and no annotations, units or footnotes beyond the header. Reading the table shows two consistent monotonic trends: within any row, lnZ decreases steadily as temperature increases (e.g. 64.08 at 900 °C down to 52.01 at 1150 °C for 0.01 s⁻¹), and within any column, lnZ increases as strain rate increases (e.g. 64.08, 66.38, 68.69, 70.99 in the 900 °C column). The extreme entries are 70.99 (10 s⁻¹, 900 °C) and 52.01 (0.01 s⁻¹, 1150 °C). The table demonstrates that the Zener-Hollomon parameter tracks the hot-deformation severity, rising with strain rate and falling with temperature exactly as the flow stress does, which is why Z is used to normalise the characteristic stress-strain values.

observations.observation: The table stub column is labelled ε̇ (s⁻¹) and lists four strain rates: 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10.
The column head is labelled T (°C) and spans six temperatures: 900, 950, 1000, 1050, 1100 and 1150.
Row ε̇ = 0.01 s⁻¹ prints lnZ = 64.08, 61.27, 58.69, 56.29, 54.08 and 52.01 at 900-1150 °C respectively, i.e. it decreases monotonically with temperature.
Within the 900 °C column lnZ increases with strain rate: 64.08 (0.01 s⁻¹), 66.38 (0.1 s⁻¹), 68.69 (1 s⁻¹), 70.99 (10 s⁻¹).
The largest printed value is 70.99 (10 s⁻¹, 900 °C) and the smallest is 52.01 (0.01 s⁻¹, 1150 °C); all 24 cells are filled and no cell is blank.
The caption identifies the table as the lnZ value of Fe-Mn-Al–C steel under different T and strain rate.
The Z parameter increases with increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature, the same trend as the flow stress.
The Z values were obtained from the calculated dynamic recrystallization activation energy together with formula (3).
The Zener-Hollomon parameter is used to build functional relationships between Z and the characteristic values εc/σc, εp/σp and εs/σs of the flow-stress curves.
